conflicts.point: Whether decentralized open-source iteration can safely manage the security risks of frontier AI systems without centralized pre-deployment safety evaluations.

positions.stance: Decentralized adversarial review patches vulnerabilities and surfaces security flaws faster than institutional committees, making pre-deployment restrictions unnecessary and counterproductive.
Frontier model deployments carry irreversible risks that cannot be patched post-hoc like traditional software, requiring mandatory pre-release verification by external authorities.

verdicts.conflict: Whether decentralized open-source iteration can safely manage the security risks of frontier AI systems without centralized pre-deployment safety evaluations.
verdicts.rationale: Safety advocates account for the permanence of capability diffusion once model weights are distributed across decentralized networks. Opposing arguments treat AI models like conventional software that can be patched post-hoc, ignoring the unique challenges of recalling decentralized digital artifacts with dual-use capabilities.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical evidence showing that advanced frontier models with autonomous replication capabilities can be successfully recalled or contained after widespread decentralized distribution.
